scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the one at fault (AITA) in this situation. Let me go through the scenario step by step to understand what happened and why my boyfriend suggested breaking up. First, I'm a Christian, and I want to approach this with love and understanding. My partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm, and I have a weekend job from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together but are local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. My son, who is 12, decided he wanted to play football on weekends and was really excited about it. Initially, I thought of asking my boyfriend to pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom, she strongly expected me to pay, saying it was my responsibility, not his. Even though he's been in my life for three years, I ended up paying for it. To afford this, I extended my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends. He looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's job." I snapped at him, telling him that his dad lives in South London, while we're in North London, and his dad doesn't drive. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. He got really angry, saying he had to work longer hours to support me and my son and wanted to use his weekends for football games, etc., since I wasn't home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him too quickly. He then suggested we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. I was shocked and replied, "Really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world, love!" The little sneak then went to my mom, had a heart-to-heart with her, which ended up in her calling me and telling me I was out of line. Now, I'm wondering if I'm the one at fault here. Let me break this down. My son wanted to play football, which is a positive thing. I took the responsibility to pay for it, which is commendable. However, I extended my work hours to afford it, which might have caused stress. Then, I asked my boyfriend for help with transportation, which he refused, leading to an argument. I snapped at him, which might have been a mistake. I made him feel responsible for something he might not have felt was his duty, especially since my mom expected me to handle it. He felt burdened by the additional responsibilities and wanted his weekends free, which is understandable. I think the main issues here are communication and expectations. I didn't discuss the financial and logistical aspects with him before making decisions. I assumed he would help, but he felt it wasn't his responsibility. My mom's involvement added pressure, making me feel like I had to handle everything alone, which might have led to me overstepping. I also snapped at him, which could have hurt his feelings and made him feel unappreciated. He might have felt that I didn't value his contributions, leading him to feel the relationship was too one-sided. In terms of AITA, I think I might have been too demanding without considering his feelings and responsibilities. I didn't communicate my needs clearly and assumed he would help without discussing it. However, he also didn't express his feelings clearly and suggested a breakup over something that could have been resolved with better communication. As a Christian, I should consider forgiveness and understanding. Maybe I should reflect on how I communicated and whether I could have handled the situation differently. It's also important to consider mutual respect and shared responsibilities in a relationship. So, in conclusion, while I might have been too demanding, he also reacted impulsively. Both parties could have handled the situation better with open communication and mutual understanding.
